en: to be used; to be applied

examples.en: This app is used all over the world.
This room used to be used as a meeting room.

examples.ko: 이 도구는 요리할 때만 사용되는 것이 아니에요.
examples.en: This tool isn't used only when cooking.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 편지에서 자주 사용돼서 알아 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: This word is often used in letters, so it's good to know.

examples.ko: 앞으로 이 건물은 도서관으로 사용될 거예요.
examples.en: From now on, this building will be used as a library.

examples.ko: 버려지지 않고 다시 사용되면 환경에 좋아요.
examples.en: If things are reused instead of thrown away, it's good for the environment.

explain: '사용하다'는 사람이 쓰는 것이고, '사용되다'는 쓰이는 물건이나 말이 주어예요. 설명서·뉴스·보고서에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '쓰여요'(쓰이다)를 더 많이 써요. 도구·말·돈에는 '사용', 시설·서비스에는 '이용'이 어울려요.

phrases.en: This word is often used in daily life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사용되다'와 같은 뜻이에요. 말할 때는 '쓰이다'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 사용되다; 쓰이다 is more common in speech.

phrases.en: This app is widely used in schools.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널리'를 붙이면 많은 곳에서 쓰인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 널리 means it is used in many places.

phrases.en: That room is not being used now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'를 붙여 쓰이지 않는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -지 않다 to say it is not in use.

explain_en: Neutral, slightly formal: something serves a purpose (회의실로 사용돼요) '사용하다' is a person using something; with '사용되다' the thing or word being used is the subject. You see it in manuals, news and reports. In speech, '쓰여요' (쓰이다) is more common. Use '사용' for tools, words and money, and '이용' for facilities and services.

gh: used as a means; may imply exploitation

p.n: 쓰이다 is a more everyday, spoken-sounding word.

t90.ax: This app is used all over the world.

examples.en: My brother is quiet, but I am a chatterbox.
My friend is an incurable chatterbox.

examples.ko: 수다쟁이 동생 덕분에 집이 늘 시끌시끌해요.
examples.en: Thanks to my chatty younger sibling, the house is always noisy.

examples.ko: 우리 반 수다쟁이가 오늘은 웬일로 조용해요.
examples.en: For some reason, the chatterbox of our class is quiet today.

examples.ko: 수다쟁이 할머니가 이웃 이야기를 다 알고 계세요.
examples.en: The chatty grandmother knows all the stories about the neighbors.

examples.ko: 저는 원래 수다쟁이가 아닌데 그 사람 앞에서는 말이 많아져요.
examples.en: I am not normally a chatterbox, but I talk a lot in front of that person.

explain: '멋쟁이', '고집쟁이'처럼 '-쟁이'가 붙은 말이라 친근하거나 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 윗사람에게 직접 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요. 성격을 부드럽게 말할 때는 '말이 많다', '수다스럽다'를 써요.

phrases.en: When I meet my friends, I become a chatterbox.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정한 사람 앞에서 말이 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you talk a lot around certain people.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is chatty, so the house is noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 직접 놀리는 느낌이 적어서 더 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels less like teasing, so it sounds gentler.

phrases.example: 저는 친한 친구 앞에서는 말이 많아요.
phrases.en: I talk a lot in front of close friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격이나 상황을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to casually describe a personality or situation.

explain_en: Like '멋쟁이' and '고집쟁이', the '-쟁이' ending gives it a friendly or teasing tone. It can be rude to use directly about someone older. For a softer description, say '말이 많다' or '수다스럽다'.

examples.en: Who is it this round?
I lost at rock-paper-scissors, so I became the seeker.
The seeker closes their eyes and counts to ten.
Hide quickly so the seeker doesn't catch you!
My younger sibling grumbles that they don't want to be it all the time.
We played rock-paper-scissors to decide who would be it.

explain: '술래가 되다', '술래를 정하다'처럼 써요. 숨바꼭질에서는 찾는 사람이고, 얼음땡 같은 놀이에서는 쫓아가는 사람이에요.

phrases.en: We decide who is it by rock-paper-scissors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이를 시작하기 전에 술래를 뽑을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a game to choose who is it.

phrases.en: I'll be it this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '술래가 되다'보다 자기가 하겠다고 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 술래가 되다 when volunteering.

phrases.en: If you get caught, we switch who is it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡힌 사람이 술래가 되는 규칙을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the rule that the caught player becomes it.

explain_en: It is used as '술래가 되다' (to be it) or '술래를 정하다' (to choose who is it). In hide-and-seek it is the one who searches, and in games like freeze tag it is the chaser.

examples.en: I am right-handed, but my younger sibling is left-handed.
These scissors are for right-handed people, so they're awkward for me.
If a right-hander writes with the left hand, the writing gets crooked.
Everyone in my family is right-handed.
I'm right-handed, so my right shoulder often hurts.
Most tools are made to suit right-handed people.

explain: 반대말은 '왼손잡이'이고, 손이 아니라 그런 사람을 가리켜요. 도구 이름 뒤에 '용'을 붙여 '오른손잡이용'이라고 하면 오른손잡이를 위해 만든 물건이에요.

phrases.en: This mouse is for right-handed people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 이름 앞에 붙여서 오른손잡이를 위해 만든 것이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before an item to mean it is made for right-handers.

phrases.en: I'm right-handed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 어느 손을 주로 쓰는지 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which hand you mainly use.

phrases.en: There are many right-handed people in our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수를 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing numbers of people.

explain_en: The opposite is '왼손잡이'. It refers to the person, not the hand itself. Adding '용' as in '오른손잡이용' means something made for right-handed people.

examples.en: Please don't misunderstand what I said.
My friend completely misunderstood me.
People often misunderstand this word.
I'll explain in detail so there's no misunderstanding.
I'm sorry I misheard and misunderstood.
If you misunderstood my text message, I'm sorry.

explain: 사람의 마음이나 말을 잘못 받아들였을 때 써요. 명사 '오해'로 '오해를 풀다', '오해를 사다'처럼 쓰는 일도 많아요. '오해하지 마세요'는 아주 자주 쓰는 표현이라 통째로 외워 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Please don't misunderstand me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 자주 쓰는 표현이라 통째로 외워 두면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common expression worth memorizing as a whole.

phrases.en: I met my friend and cleared up the misunderstanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못 알았던 일을 바로잡을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for correcting a misunderstanding.

phrases.en: I misunderstood that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 잘못 받아들인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for having taken something the wrong way.

explain_en: Everyday — misread someone's words or intent (말을 오해하다) Use it when you take someone's feelings or words the wrong way. The noun '오해' is also common in '오해를 풀다' (clear up a misunderstanding) and '오해를 사다' (be misunderstood). '오해하지 마세요' is a very common expression, so it is worth memorizing as a whole.

examples.ko: 이다음에 시간 되면 또 같이 와요.
examples.en: Let's come again together next time when we have time.
You can get off at the next stop.
Next is my turn to present.
Next time I'll make sure not to be late.
I'm worried about what comes next and I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 이다음 주에는 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: It looks like it will rain the week after this.

explain: '이다음에'는 '나중에, 훗날'처럼 막연한 앞날이나 다음 기회를 말할 때 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '다음에'나 '나중에'도 많이 써요. 순서를 말할 때는 '이다음 정류장'처럼 바로 뒤의 것을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: Let's go on a trip together sometime later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막연한 앞날의 기회를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a vague future opportunity.

phrases.en: I'll get off at the next stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 뒤에 오는 것을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points to the one coming right after this.

phrases.en: Let's talk again later.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다음에'와 비슷하고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '이다음에' and more common in daily speech.

explain_en: Spoken, next occasion after the present one (이다음에 만나요) '이다음에' is often used for a vague future or the next chance, like 'later' or 'someday'. In daily talk '다음에' and '나중에' are also common. For order, it points to the one right after this, as in '이다음 정류장' (the stop after this).

t90.ax: Next is my turn to present.

examples.en: Hey, what do you think you're doing?
The boss called out, 'Hey, Assistant Manager Kim!'
In the drama, he shouted, 'Hey! Stop right there!'

examples.ko: 아저씨가 '이봐 학생' 하고 저를 불러 세웠어요.
examples.en: A man called out 'Hey, student' and stopped me.

examples.ko: '이봐, 이봐!' 하고 누가 저를 계속 불러요.
examples.en: Someone keeps calling me, 'Hey, hey!'

examples.ko: 옛날 영화에서는 '이봐, 친구' 하고 말을 거는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: In old movies there are scenes where someone says, 'Hey, pal.'

explain: 친구나 아랫사람을 부를 때 쓰는 말투라서, 윗사람이나 처음 보는 어른에게 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요. 낯선 사람을 정중하게 부를 때는 '저기요'를 써요.

phrases.example: 이봐요, 여기서 담배 피우면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Hey, you can't smoke here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이봐'보다 조금 공손하지만 낯선 사람에게는 여전히 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more polite than '이봐', but can still sound rough to strangers.

phrases.en: Excuse me, could you tell me the way?
phrases.nuance_ko: 낯선 사람이나 어른을 정중하게 부를 때 써서 '이봐'보다 안전해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to call a stranger or an elder, safer than '이봐'.

phrases.en: My friend called me, saying 'Hey, wait a second!'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 상대를 멈추게 하려고 짧게 덧붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short add-on between close friends to make someone stop.

explain_en: It is used to call a friend or someone younger or lower in rank, so with an elder or a stranger it can sound rude. To politely get a stranger's attention, use '저기요'.

examples.ko: 동생은 주말마다 열두 시까지 자는 잠꾸러기예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a sleepyhead who sleeps until noon every weekend.
I'm a sleepyhead, so I'm always late for morning appointments.
My son is a sleepyhead, so he's hard to wake up.
Hey sleepyhead, get up now!

examples.ko: 저는 잠꾸러기가 아니고 밤에 일하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: I'm not a sleepyhead, I'm someone who works at night.
I found out after marriage that my husband is a sleepyhead.

explain: 잠이 많은 사람을 귀엽게 놀릴 때 써요. 아이나 가까운 사이에 쓰고, 어른에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요. '장난꾸러기', '욕심꾸러기'처럼 '-꾸러기'가 붙은 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: My sleepyhead little brother overslept again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이나 가까운 사람 앞에 붙여서 귀엽게 놀리는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put it before a family member or close person to tease them in a cute way.

phrases.en: My friend teases me by calling me a sleepyhead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠이 많은 사람을 장난스럽게 놀릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when playfully teasing someone who sleeps a lot.
phrases.en_equiv: to tease someone as a sleepyhead

phrases.en: My son is a total sleepyhead.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전'을 붙이면 잠이 아주 많다는 뜻이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '완전' makes it stronger: the person sleeps a lot.

explain_en: It is used to tease someone affectionately for sleeping a lot. Use it with children or close people; saying it directly to an adult can be rude. Other words with '-꾸러기' include '장난꾸러기' and '욕심꾸러기'.

examples.en: A west-facing living room is nice because the evening glow is beautiful.
I walked along the riverside watching the sunset glow.
The sky was dyed red by the evening glow.
We took photos under the evening glow.

examples.ko: 저녁노을은 날씨가 맑은 날 더 예뻐요.
examples.en: The evening glow is prettier on clear days.
The evening glow is settling over the sea.

explain: '노을'만 써도 되고, '저녁노을'은 해가 질 때라는 점을 분명히 해요. 아침에 보이는 노을은 '아침노을'이라고 해요. '노을이 지다', '노을이 물들다'가 어울리는 짝이에요.

phrases.en: The sunset glow in the sky is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '저녁노을'보다 짧고, 시간대를 따로 말하지 않아도 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than '저녁노을', and used when you don't need to say the time of day.

phrases.en: I watched the sea as the evening glow set.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 붉어지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes the sky turning red as the sun sets.

phrases.en: The sky dyed with the evening glow was really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하늘의 색을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe the color of the sky.
phrases.en_equiv: sky tinted by the evening glow

explain_en: Red sky at sunset; scenery, descriptive. '노을' alone is fine; '저녁노을' makes clear it is at sunset. The glow seen in the morning is '아침노을'. Natural pairings are '노을이 지다' and '노을이 물들다'.

examples.en: In summer, thin pants are cool and comfortable.

examples.ko: 이 쇼핑몰은 팬츠 종류가 정말 다양해요.
examples.en: This online store has a really wide variety of pants.

examples.ko: 검은 팬츠에 흰 셔츠를 입고 면접에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the interview in black pants and a white shirt.

examples.ko: 키가 작아서 팬츠 길이를 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: I am short, so I need to shorten the length of my pants.

examples.ko: 운동할 때는 잘 늘어나는 팬츠를 입어요.
examples.en: When I work out, I wear pants that stretch well.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서 팬츠 두 벌을 사면 한 벌은 할인해 줘요.
examples.en: If you buy two pairs of pants at that shop, one is discounted.

explain: 가게나 상품 이름에서는 '팬츠'를 많이 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 보통 '바지'라고 해요. '팬티'는 속옷이라서 서로 바꿔 쓰면 안 돼요.

phrases.en: I wore comfortable pants today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팬츠'와 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '바지'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 팬츠; 바지 is more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: Wide-leg pants are nice and cool in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통이 넓은 바지예요. 옷 가게나 쇼핑몰에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pants with a wide leg, often seen in shops and online stores.

phrases.en: I wear sweatpants when I exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동할 때 입는 편한 바지예요. '운동복 바지'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Comfortable pants for exercise, like sweatpants or track pants; also called '운동복 바지'.

explain_en: Shops and product names often use '팬츠', while everyday speech usually says '바지'. '팬티' means underwear, so the two cannot be swapped.

t90.ax: In summer, thin pants are cool and comfortable.

examples.en: I took out a sledgehammer to break a big rock.
This hammer is much heavier than I expected.
My hand hurt after hitting the wall with a hammer.
The nail struck by the hammer went in deep.
Both the hammer and the screwdriver are in the toolbox.

examples.ko: 육상 대회에서 해머 던지기 경기를 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the hammer throw event at the athletics meet.

explain: '해머'는 크고 무거운 망치예요. 보통 망치는 '망치'라고 해요. 육상 종목 '해머던지기'에서도 '해머'를 써요.

phrases.en: I hit the wall with a hammer and broke it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 무거운 망치로 세게 칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for hitting hard with a big, heavy hammer.

phrases.en: The hammer throw is a track and field event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 종목 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of an athletic event.

phrases.en: He lifted the heavy hammer with ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 해머를 손에 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for lifting a heavy hammer by hand.

explain_en: 해머 is a big, heavy hammer. An ordinary hammer is called 망치. In the track-and-field event 해머던지기, 해머 is also the word used.

examples.en: If you follow the arrows, you will reach the exit.
The arrow drawn on the road points to the right.
I move through the menu with the arrow keys on the keyboard.
I marked the route on the map with a red arrow.
What does this arrow mean?
If you touch the arrow, the screen moves on.

explain: 방향을 알려 주는 '→' 모양을 가리켜요. '화살표를 따라가다', '화살표로 표시하다'처럼 말해요. '느낌표', '물음표'처럼 '-표'로 끝나는 부호 이름이기도 해요.

phrases.en: I marked the road with an arrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방향이나 위치를 그림으로 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing a direction or place with a drawing.

phrases.en: Please walk in the direction of the arrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 길을 알려 줄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in signs and directions.

phrases.en: If you press the up arrow, it goes up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 기계의 화살표 버튼을 누를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pressing arrow buttons on a computer or machine.

explain_en: It names the → shape that shows direction. You say 화살표를 따라가다 or 화살표로 표시하다. Like 느낌표 and 물음표, it ends in -표, the suffix for a sign or mark.
